work_order.debate_summary: Accepted blocking B1: journal-less baseline means db:generate re-emits the ledger table without IF NOT EXISTS and breaks every boot against migrate.ts:53; work order requires hand-reviewed 0002 with no ledger DDL plus fresh double-boot proof. Accepted M1 signup oracle: duplicate-email error is enumerable, so signup must return identical success whether or not the address exists (race mapped the same way). Accepted M2 IP spoofing in part: x-forwarded-for first-entry is client-controlled, so per-normalized-email is the primary key and IP is a hint with defensive parsing. Downgraded M3: per-instance throttling is a documented v1 limitation, not a TR-6 failure; kept in-memory, recorded as residual risk. Accepted M4: one withDb per server action enforces the decided one-Pool-per-request lifecycle. Accepted M5: SESSION_SECRET must pepper the token hash rather than sit dead behind the prod boot guard. Softened M6: no ui.md profile contract exists, so AC-5 claims Auth-pattern conformance only for sign-in/up and tokens/a11y reuse for profile. Accepted M7: preserved input needs controlled inputs in the client island. Accepted minors m1 (add validation.ts module), m2 (drop deprecated @types/bcryptjs), m4 (normalize at the validation boundary, not just the limiter), m5 (map unique-violation race to neutral response). Dismissed m3: package-lock.json exists in the repo root, so the npm-ci claim is factually wrong.

issue_snapshot.title: Email and password accounts with sessions and profile
issue_snapshot.body:
A real person can sign up, sign in, sign out and keep a profile, giving every later group flow a trusted identity.

Person sees: Auth screens (sign-up and sign-in card with email, password, show and hide toggle, submit; profile with display name and default currency) with neutral errors and pending states. Contract: DEFINES the lib/auth session contract (bcryptjs cost 12, opaque random tokens stored server-side, httpOnly Secure-in-production SameSite=Lax cookies, server-side revocation on sign-out, rate-limited sign-in) that every later group scope consumes as sessionUser. Constraints: TR-6 with no email enumeration; human decision for hand-rolled sessions stands.

**Risk.** Auth and security risk: bcryptjs cost 12, opaque server-side sessions with sign-out revocation, httpOnly Secure SameSite cookies, rate-limited sign-in, enumeration-safe errors.

**Out of scope**
- Group creation and invites
- Expenses, balances and activity feeds
- Password reset and account deletion (spec S-10 deferral)

Covers: TR-6, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #3.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Sign up with email and password, see neutral errors that never reveal whether an email is registered, and land signed in with a profile holding display name and default currency
- **IAC-2** Sign out ends the session server-side so the old cookie authorizes nothing; sign in again works and failed sign-ins are rate-limited
- **IAC-3** Auth pages are mobile-first from the token set with labelled controls, visible focus, preserved input on error and no double-submit

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.
